claims.claim: Innoviz's automotive-grade LiDAR capability can bridge from long-cycle vehicle qualification into defense/security sensing needs, where counter-UAS and perimeter applications create a second demand path.
The structural bottleneck is not sensing need alone but conversion of qualified technology into recurring volume programs at economics sufficient to fund the company.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Automotive-grade sensing and perception capability is differentiated, but deployment success and customer program conversion remain external bottlenecks.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Defense diversification reduces dependence on automotive timing, yet both markets require customer qualification and recurring orders.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: LiDAR provides precise 3D sensing, but radar, cameras and sensor fusion architectures can substitute in some applications.

causalEdges.mechanism: vehicles and defense systems require reliable object/location information under operational constraints
causalEdges.falsifier: alternative sensor stacks meet required performance at materially better lifecycle economics

causalEdges.mechanism: qualified sensors can be repurposed into counter-UAS, perimeter and situational-awareness systems
causalEdges.falsifier: initial deployments fail operational validation or do not generate follow-on orders

causalEdges.mechanism: customer validation can convert initial orders into repeat units and SOP volume
causalEdges.falsifier: collaborations remain pilots or program timing slips without recurring material orders

risks.risk: Sensor substitution can cap addressable value even where perception demand grows.
The successor bottleneck is customer conversion and volume economics rather than technical capability alone.

unknowns.unknown: Recurring defense reorder rate and mature automotive program unit economics remain unproven in current lineage.

claims.claim: Record Q2 revenue and initial defense orders demonstrate commercial traction, but Q2 operating loss remained $18.4 million and liquidity before the July financing was about $48.5 million, so financing/dilution remains a material present risk.

factors.name: financingRisk
factors.basis: Operating losses and a July registered direct offering show external capital remains relevant before self-funded economics are established.

factors.name: concentrationRisk
factors.basis: Large automotive programs and early defense orders depend on a limited number of customer program decisions and deployment outcomes.

factors.name: confidenceInflation
factors.basis: Six engagements and prospective-customer conversations should not be equated with recurring production revenue.

risks.risk: Cash burn and equity financing can dilute shareholders before durable positive operating economics.
Initial defense orders are contingent evidence: additional units depend on successful first deployment.
Automotive SOP schedules can slip and alternative sensor stacks can pressure volumes/pricing.

contradictions.claim: Commercial traction is improving while operating economics remain loss-making.
contradictions.resolution: Both are supported; traction strengthens the thesis but does not remove financing risk.

unknowns.unknown: Cash runway after ongoing burn and the July financing, absent later financial statements, is not established here.
